question: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) in a Spring Boot application. Explain the difference between RBAC and attribute-based access control (ABAC).

keyPoints: RBAC assigns permissions to roles, users inherit permissions through role membership
Spring Security uses @PreAuthorize, @Secured annotations for method-level security
ABAC makes decisions based on attributes (user, resource, environment), more flexible than RBAC
RBAC simpler to implement and manage, ABAC better for fine-grained complex policies
Consider hierarchical roles for large organizations
expectedAnswer.explanation: RBAC groups permissions into roles (ADMIN, USER, MANAGER). Users are assigned roles, simplifying permission management. Spring Security integrates RBAC through UserDetailsService loading granted authorities. ABAC evaluates policies based on attributes: user department, resource classification, time of day, etc. ABAC offers more flexibility (e.g., 'allow if user.department == resource.department AND time < 18:00') but requires policy engine and is more complex. Choose RBAC for straightforward hierarchical permissions, ABAC for dynamic complex rules.

followUps: How would you implement permission inheritance in a role hierarchy?
What are the performance implications of fine-grained authorization checks?
